title: Prove shared-D controller rank loss with productive helper reuse
body:
This scoped negative result proves that a common-D controller cannot gain a favorable raw power moment in the stated characteristic-two FULL/THIN alphabet, even when it reuses productive H8 helpers and mixes scalar coordinates across ports. It closes a proposed way to remove idle calls. It does not improve the complete kappa calculation or change the selected frontier.

The [proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/efc8f93d1d3c911f61784c70a4feb6ed7b372b43/research/reused-d-helper-rank-bound/PROOF.md), [exact receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/efc8f93d1d3c911f61784c70a4feb6ed7b372b43/research/reused-d-helper-rank-bound/RESULT.json), [source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/efc8f93d1d3c911f61784c70a4feb6ed7b372b43/research/reused-d-helper-rank-bound/SOURCES.json) and [validation record](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/efc8f93d1d3c911f61784c70a4feb6ed7b372b43/research/reused-d-helper-rank-bound/VALIDATION.md) define the result and its limits.

For n actual fields, f FULL calls with v main pairs each, s reused full-rank helper occurrences and h paid thin H1 calls, coefficient comparison and the classical rank inequality give `M=2vf+s>=n` and `h>=2n-2vf-2s`. The complete compact BIT invoice then has rank surplus at most `-63f`. Retaining its four H4 helper credits gives the exact bound `Delta_t<=-47f*8^(t-1)<0` for every `0<=t<=1`. The helper counts may be unequal and need not be multiples of 111. The favorable proposed family `n/v=2p, f=p+2, h/v=p-1` needs p<=3 for its endpoint and p>=66 for its relaxed rank price; these conditions cannot both hold.

The alphabet requires four independent coefficients in `F[q,d]/(q^2,d^2)`, one shared D, the explicit FULL support/defect ranks, funded thin ranks and ordinary constant scalar changes of basis. It excludes distinct fresh D variables, productive thin outputs, different native calls and operator-valued free codes. The existing compact source controller uses distinct fresh D blocks. Its retained positive rank surplus 753 is checked as a control and is not ruled out.

All consumed files are present at the publication base `32890bc5de034ab8fc93ac88ead7279a6a416d04`. That checkpoint's selected conditional kappa is 0.003027288235 under its existing assumptions. The [compact source receipt](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/32890bc5de034ab8fc93ac88ead7279a6a416d04/research/bit-compact-productive-controller/RESULT.json) supplies the native local profile. The checker independently joins it to the complete saved 18-FULL invoice; it does not rerun the source native construction.

Python 3.12 or later and the standard library suffice:

```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/reused-d-helper-rank-bound
python3 -I -O -B research/reused-d-helper-rank-bound/verify.py
```

Expected token: `PASS_SHARED_D_HELPER_REUSE_RANK_BOUND`. Normal and optimized checks passed, including 13 exact four-coefficient attaining examples, four rejected endpoint mutations, the separate missing-helper-debit calculation, 75 integer relaxations and the shared signed-invoice comparison. A Git-free read-only export with empty PATH passed both modes with all input hashes unchanged. Committed-byte and export-integrity checks passed for 13 files. The strict source-history check stopped because the checkout is shallow; full-history preflight remains open. No selected cold replay, physical supplier admission, compiler, Lean proof, hosted CI or complete multiplication theorem check ran.

The [source credit notice](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/32890bc5de034ab8fc93ac88ead7279a6a416d04/research/bit-compact-productive-controller/README.md#credit) credits ai-nanachi's compact436 word from [PR #4326](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4326), its partial productive interface, Cinna Davis's query-thinned controllers in [PR #4440](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4440) and [PR #4470](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4470), and the retained zxv, Jacob Alan Sussman, [PR #589](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/589), geometry, framing, COPY, compiler and analytic lineage. Those interfaces are inherited. The [shared invoice checker](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/32890bc5de034ab8fc93ac88ead7279a6a416d04/scripts/compare_recursive_invoices.py) supplies the existing concave-order comparison.

The campaign's BIT worker supplied the first projector-factor proof; its branching worker supplied the productive-helper extension. This package gives their common field-count formulation and complete partial-helper power bound. Two other campaign workers reviewed the algebra; one also ran an independent 448-field, cross-port fixture with helper counts 1 and 3. These are author-side AI checks. Prepared for Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0. No independent human acceptance or proof-assistant verification is claimed.

Related [PR #5507](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5507) extends [PR #5456](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5456) to two-owner multigraphs under independent stage-axis assumptions. The present proof has one shared D and arbitrary constant scalar coupling; it does not impose a two-owner coordinate support graph. These are different restricted alphabets.
